newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan PM proposes peace talks with India.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan PM proposes peace talks with India.

text.p: Pakistan's new Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif on Thursday proposed talks with his Indian counterpart H.D. Deve Gowda to settle a dispute over the Kashmir region.

Sharif said in a letter to Deve Gowda, copies of which were released by the Pakistani Foreign Ministry in Islamabad, that their meeting should be preceded by preparatory talks between the foreign ministry secretaries of the two countries.
Sharif's letter was responding to one sent by Deve Gowda on February 17 to congratulate the Pakistani prime minister on taking office and proposing a resumption of peace talks.
Pakistan and India have fought three wars since independence from Britain in 1947, two of them over Kashmir.

"In this context, I am encouraged by your willingness for wide-ranging and comprehensive talks on all issues of mutual concern," Sharif's letter said. But it added: "I hope you will agree with me that without some progress on the core issue of Jammu and Kashmir, it will be difficult to initiate meaningful cooperation in economic and cultural fields."
Sharif proposed that foreign secretary-level talks be held preferably before the end of March to prepare ground for meaningful discussions between the two prime ministers.
